intro: Doha rewards visitors with world-class museums, a buzzing souq and easy desert escapes. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Doha Metro has three lines (Red, Gold, Green); Msheireb is the main transfer station.
Metro fares are about QR 2 per trip and QR 6 for a day pass; VIP cars cost more.
Free metrolink feeder buses connect stations to nearby areas.
Karwa and Al Million are main taxis; Uber works well in Doha.
Buses are cheap but infrequent and often late; route maps are hard to read.
Driving is on the right; traffic jams and roadworks are common. A free tram runs in Lusail and Msheireb Downtown.

souq-waqif.name: Souq Waqif
souq-waqif.price_text: Free to enter · pay per purchase
souq-waqif.hours: Shops roughly 10:00–22:00 · many restaurants later · quieter in the morning
souq-waqif.tip: Come after sunset when the lanes fill up, and bargain politely in the spice and fabric sections.

mia.name: Museum of Islamic Art, Doha
mia.price_text: ≈ QAR 50 for adults · check current rate and free days online
mia.hours: Closed Tuesday · otherwise roughly 09:00–19:00, later on weekends
mia.tip: The lakeside terrace and the MIA Park lawn give the best skyline photos.

pearl.name: The Pearl-Qatar
pearl.price_text: Free to walk · cafes and shops extra
pearl.hours: Marina and promenade open all day · restaurants into the night
pearl.tip: Walk the marina at sunset, then eat at Porto Arabia. It is a taxi ride from the old centre.

nmq.name: National Museum of Qatar
nmq.price_text: ≈ QAR 50 for adults · check current rate online
nmq.tip: The building itself is the attraction. Allow time for the film and the desert galleries.

katara.name: Katara Cultural Village
katara.price_text: Free to enter · some shows and events ticketed
katara.hours: Grounds open all day · shops and cafes roughly 10:00–22:00
katara.tip: See the amphitheatre and the blue mosque, then walk to the beach. Check the events calendar first.

corniche.name: Doha Corniche
corniche.tip: Walk or cycle the 7 km curve at sunset for the full skyline. Take a short dhow ride from the Souq Waqif end.

kidzania.name: KidZania (Doha)
kidzania.price_text: ≈ QAR 100–150 per child · check current tickets online
kidzania.hours: Usually daily, roughly 10:00–22:00 · check on the day
kidzania.tip: Best for ages 4–12. Book online and go on a weekday to avoid queues.

lusail-stadium.name: Lusail Stadium
lusail-stadium.price_text: Tours and events priced separately · check on the day
lusail-stadium.hours: Only open for matches, events or booked tours · check on the day
lusail-stadium.tip: It is far north of the city. Go only if there is a match or a booked tour, and arrange transport back.

machboos.name: Machboos
machboos.price_text: ≈ QAR 35–70 a plate at casual restaurants
machboos.hours: Lunch and dinner · most restaurants roughly 12:00–23:00
machboos.tip: Qatar's national rice dish with chicken, lamb or fish. Try it at a local restaurant near Souq Waqif.

souq-market.name: Souq Waqif food and spice lanes
souq-market.price_text: Free to browse · snacks from a few QAR
souq-market.tip: Graze your way through: dates, spices, fresh juice and grilled meat. Cash helps in small stalls.

mia-park.name: MIA Park and skyline viewpoint
mia-park.hours: Open daily · best light around sunset
mia-park.tip: The lawn and pier give the classic West Bay skyline shot. Bring water in summer.

dhow-cruise.name: Corniche dhow cruise
dhow-cruise.price_text: ≈ QAR 80–150 per person · negotiate and confirm duration
dhow-cruise.tip: A short wooden-dhow ride shows the skyline from the water. Agree the price and time before boarding.

msheireb.name: Msheireb Downtown walk
msheireb.price_text: Free · museums in the district may charge
msheireb.hours: Streets open all day · cafes into the evening
msheireb.tip: A restored old-town quarter with calm streets and cafes. Good for a shaded walk between sights.

souq-waqif-camel.name: Camel and horse stables at Souq Waqif
souq-waqif-camel.price_text: Free to look · rides extra if offered
souq-waqif-camel.tip: A short walk from the souq. Go early morning to see the animals being exercised.

katara-beach.name: Katara beach
katara-beach.price_text: ≈ QAR 50 entry · check current rate on the day
katara-beach.hours: Daylight hours · check on the day
katara-beach.tip: A small managed beach inside Katara. Confirm entry price and swimming hours before you go.

west-bay-view.name: West Bay skyline viewpoint
west-bay-view.tip: Walk the West Bay promenade for close-up views of the towers. Best at dusk.

porto-arabia.name: Porto Arabia marina walk
porto-arabia.price_text: Free to walk · food and shops extra
porto-arabia.hours: All day · liveliest in the evening
porto-arabia.tip: Yachts, cafes and a Mediterranean feel. Good for an evening stroll and dinner.

souq-waqif-restaurants.name: Souq Waqif restaurant row
souq-waqif-restaurants.tip: Many casual and traditional restaurants sit side by side. Book ahead on weekends.

mia-cafe.name: Museum of Islamic Art cafe terrace
mia-cafe.price_text: ≈ QAR 40–80 for coffee and a snack
mia-cafe.tip: Sit outside for skyline views. Check museum opening days first.

souq-waqif-shopping.name: Souq Waqif fabric and craft shops
souq-waqif-shopping.price_text: Free to browse · pay per item
souq-waqif-shopping.tip: Good for textiles, perfume and small gifts. Compare a few stalls before buying.

corniche-cycle.name: Corniche cycle or run
corniche-cycle.hours: Early morning and evening are coolest
corniche-cycle.tip: The flat waterfront path is popular with runners. Go early to beat the heat.

katara-shows.name: Katara amphitheatre and galleries
katara-shows.price_text: Free to view · shows ticketed · check on the day
katara-shows.hours: Grounds all day · event times vary
katara-shows.tip: Check the Katara events calendar for concerts and exhibitions during your stay.

stays.why: Modern towers and the Corniche on the doorstep; easy metro to the airport and sights.
Sleep in the old heart: market lanes, restaurants and the corniche walk at night.
Quiet new downtown next to Souq Waqif; main metro transfer at Msheireb station.
Marina living, cafés and a beach feel; good for longer stays and families.

food: Try Qatari dishes: machboos (spiced rice with meat or fish), harees and luqaimat dumplings with date syrup.
Souq Waqif is the easy first stop: grilled fish, Lebanese mezze and shisha courtyards in the evening.
Cheap eats: shawarma, karak tea and Indian or Pakistani cafeterias, often around QR 10–30 a meal.
Book a hotel brunch or a waterfront dinner at The Pearl or Katara for a special night.
Alcohol is served only in licensed hotel bars and restaurants. Dress modestly in public places.
more_time: Add a desert day: dune drive and Inland Sea views south of the city. Book a tour; check prices on the day.
Swap a city afternoon for Katara Cultural Village: beach, galleries and the mosque with blue tiles.
Take the metro to Education City for the National Library and campus architecture.
